title: Folding Prefill Conductor and Quant Stowage: shape-aware prefill + quant packing
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Production inference workload analysis for several enterprise tenants showed high variance in small interactive requests (median tokens < 32) that repeatedly blocked larger batch lanes and inflated per-token cost. This PR introduces a 'folding prefill conductor' that groups and shapes low-latency requests into compact micro-batches when safe, and a complementary 'quant stowage' feature that packs lightweight model subgraphs into targeted quant profiles to reduce memory pressure and improve throughput. Goals: 1) reduce unit-econ for small-chat workloads without degrading tail-latency SLOs; 2) provide deterministic simulation tooling so operators can validate before enabling tenant-wide; 3) surface observability hooks and rollout guardrails.

Summary of changes: single-line overview of the main commits and surface files changed. - Runtime: introduce prefill folding scheduler (go/runtime/prefill/folder.go), shaping policy (go/runtime/prefill/shape_policy.go), and scheduler tests. - Quant: add quant stowage registry and packer (py/quant/stowage.py), stowage heuristics and unit tests. - CLI/sim: add prefill-sim CLI that runs workload traces against folding and quant stowage logic (tools/prefill_sim/README.md, tools/prefill_sim/sim.py). - Console: dashboard tiles (console/dashboards/prefill-folding.json) and runtime metric labels. - Docs: RFC and quickstart (docs/rfc/prefill-folding-quant-stowage.md, docs/ops/enable-prefill.md).

Design notes and tradeoffs: Folding is conservative by default: we only fold requests with identical route/model/type and when predicted aggregate latency remains within the tenant SLO + buffer. The folding scheduler uses a configurable wait window (default 6ms) and an adaptive shape cap so we don't accidentally create overly long sequences. Quant stowage maps lightweight ops (prefix-only attention, short sequence MLP paths) into narrower quant profiles (4/8-bit mixed paths) using a runtime tag so we can safely fallback to full-precision for unfamiliar model variants. Both features are opt-in per-tenant and gated behind rollout flags.

Checklist (author): - [x] Implementation and unit tests for folding scheduler - [x] Quant stowage registry and heuristics - [x] Prefill sim CLI and sample traces - [x] Console tiles + docs - [x] Telemetry and metrics (fold_attempts, fold_successes, stowage_hits, stowage_fallbacks)

Release notes: Introduces an opt-in prefill folding conductor to improve micro-batch economics for small requests and a quant stowage facility to pack low-cost execution paths into compact quant profiles. Disabled by default; operators must enable per-tenant via Console or API. See docs/ops/enable-prefill.md for rollout steps and simulated dry-run guidance.

review_comments: Miguel Rios: Please add a short benchmark (p95 latency) comparing folded vs unfurled requests under 500 rps synthetic chat load. Also confirm memory overhead of tracker objects.

Asha Patel: Added prefilling microbenchmark script and updated metrics. Results included in docs/rfc/prefill-folding-quant-stowage.md (p95 improved by ~12% on sample trace). Tracker peak memory under 1.8MB per tenant for 1k concurrent folds.
Liang Chen: The adaptive shape cap is clever but could cause oscillation when traffic suddenly spikes. Can we add a conservative hysteresis and a fast-path abort if latency crosses tenant SLO?
Asha Patel: Implemented hysteresis and fast-path abort. See go/runtime/prefill/shape_policy.go + new unit test that simulates a sudden spike.
ci_checks: unit-tests: fail (flaky e2e timing test) -> reran -> pass
notes_on_rollout: Feature gated and disabled by default. Recommended rollout: 1) Dry-run simulation (tools/prefill_sim) with tenant traces; 2) Enable opt-in for a small cohort (5% tenants) with telemetry checks for fold_success_rate and p99 latency; 3) Ramp to 25% then 100% if signals stable. Automated rollback if p99 latency increases > 3% or fold_fallback_rate > 5%.
backwards_compatibility: No breaking API changes. Prefill behavior is opt-in and controlled by flags; default runtime behavior unchanged.
release_notes_short: Add opt-in prefill folding and quant stowage to reduce unit cost for small requests; disabled by default.
author_notes: This PR intentionally keeps folding conservative — it's meant as a low-risk first step so operators can experiment with tenant-level economics without large surface changes. Follow-up work: automated tenant scoring for suggested enabling and a dashboard card that shows estimated cost-savings per tenant.
testing_instructions: 1) Build runtime and start local dev cluster: make dev-up; 2) Run sample traces: python3 tools/prefill_sim/sim.py --trace tools/prefill_sim/sample_traces/tenant_chat_small.json --mode dryrun; 3) Enable flag for tenant: curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/tenant/123/flags -d '{"prefill_folding":true}' ; 4) Monitor metrics: fold_attempts, fold_successes, stowage_hits. See docs/ops/enable-prefill.md for full checklist.
estimated_impact: Based on internal sim with three sample tenants, expected unit-cost reduction of 8-16% for small-chat workloads with negligible p99 regressions when follow rollout. Quant stowage reduces memory footprint on GPU worker by ~6-9% in tests.
